conviction_note: Q3 revenue should land on the $520M guide and the ~$522M consensus. The stock turns on the Q4 guide against a ~$577-579M bar. The company's own Q4 SiPho $1B run-rate target and full wafer-start expansion support that bar. The customer read is strong: InnoLight Q3 revenue +24.6% QoQ with binding 2027 orders. Against that, the stock is down 37% from the 2026-10-06 close (258.41 to 161.36) in a sector-wide AI-optics de-rating, closed -14.1% on 10-30 on Alphabet's negative free cash flow and Intel's guide, and carries a +20.7 vol-point put skew. The Q2 beat closed +2.2% on print day and then fell 11.9% the next session. So p_up sits only slightly above 50 (53) on a large abs_move (13, above the 11.7% implied, because a Q4 guide/SiPho checkpoint after a 37% drawdown and a Friday sector crash is a big-move setup). The scaled +0.78 and the findings' sum +0.90 agree in sign and size.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue: company guide $520M +/-5% (Q2 6-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000928876/000117891326003776/exhibit_99-1.htm). Consensus $521.83M and EPS $1.07 per MarketBeat (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-tower-semiconductor-tsem-set-to-release-earnings-on-monday-2026-10-26/); 24/7 Wall St has $522.06M and normalized EPS $1.0663 (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/27/tower-semiconductors-1-2b-profit-roadmap-faces-its-biggest-test-yet-in-q3-earnings/). The two estimate sources agree, so the bar is sourced. Q4 bar (the line the stock trades on): Benzinga Q4'26E revenue $577.1M, EPS $1.26 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/TSEM/earnings-forecasts, snippet only). That matches the Q4 implied by 24/7's FY2026 consensus of $1.975B less Q1 $414M, Q2 $460M and Q3 $522M, about $579M. Release before the open on 2026-11-02 (MarketBeat, 24/7, GuruFocus); call at 10:00 ET per the company notice (https://mfn.se/all/a/tower-semiconductor/tower-semiconductor-announces-third-quarter-2026-financial-results-and-conference-call-3714efd1).
positioning_check: Short interest is about 2.5M shares, 2.2% of float, 1.6 days to cover, as of the 2026-08-19 settlement (https://equibles.com/stocks/tsem/shortinterest); it was 2.3% of float and 1.4 days in July. No October settlement was found: the Nasdaq short-interest API returned 503. This is not a crowded short. The skew is +20.68 vol points (25d put IV minus call IV), put/call OI is 1.57, and the baseline reads 'downside paid'. Event-implied move is 11.67%, straddle 15.43% to the 2026-11-06 expiry, with a wide ATM spread (25% of mid). Tape: -32.3% over 20 days, -48.6% from the 52-week high. On 2026-10-30 the stock closed at 161.36, -14.1%, on a sector shock with no company news (Benzinga, 24/7 Wall St). Sell-side: 10 analysts, Moderate Buy, $316 average target. Wedbush Hold with a $300 target on 2026-10-26. No October target cuts found. The CEO sold $25.9M on 2026-08-11.

findings.finding: Tower's own documents put Q4 2026 at roughly the ~$577-579M consensus. Its Q2 6-K says it plans to cross a $1B SiPho annual run rate in Q4 2026, i.e. at least about $250M of SiPho in the quarter, against $170M a quarter in Q2 ($680M run rate). The SiPho/SiGe wafer-start expansion completes in Q4 2026. The Q3 guide was $520M, +13% QoQ. A guide around $575-600M would meet or modestly clear the bar. The open risk is a slip in the SiPho checkpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide-led prints have moved this stock hard. Print-day close-to-close per Yahoo daily bars: 2025-11-10 +16.7% and 2026-05-13 +22.6%, both on record guides; 2026-02-11 -1.6%; 2026-08-04 +2.2%, then -11.9% the next session despite a beat and a raised 2028 model.
findings.why_not_priced: The target is public, so whether Q4 lands at or above $577M is the open question. The 37% drawdown since 2026-10-06 coincides with peer de-rating (COHR, LITE, AAOI, CRDO, ALAB), not with any Tower-specific cut. Sell-side targets average $316 with no October cuts. A market that had priced a Q4 shortfall would show estimate cuts, which do not exist.
findings.independence: This shares the bar with the InnoLight finding but rests on a different document (Tower's own 6-K versus a customer's quarterly report). The 24/7 preview (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/27/tower-semiconductors-1-2b-profit-roadmap-faces-its-biggest-test-yet-in-q3-earnings/) also cites $1.3B of signed 2027 SiPho revenue and $290M of customer prepayments.

findings.finding: InnoLight, a named Tower SiPho production partner, reported on 2026-10-29. Q3 revenue was RMB 27.77B, +24.6% QoQ and +171.8% YoY; gross margin was 46.6% versus 46.4%. Management said major overseas clients' 2027 demand is covered by binding orders. Citi kept Buy and said operating profit was in line; the net-profit miss came from FX and fair-value losses.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history of Tower reacting to InnoLight prints. InnoLight's own A-shares fell about 3% on its strong print, the sector selling good numbers (SCMP headline 'fears of slower AI growth trump upbeat earnings').
findings.why_not_priced: It landed one day before Tower closed -14.1% on 2026-10-30 alongside the US optics names, so the US tape did not reward it. Tower's Q4 guide and 2027 commentary are the first company-level place this demand can show. This is a proxy: Tower is capacity-limited, so customer demand above Tower's wafer starts adds to 2027 commentary more than to Q4 revenue. Net of the rest of the company: SiPho is roughly 35-40% of revenue, and the rest (RF, power, sensors) is covered by the ST finding.
findings.independence: Separate document from Tower's 6-K. Tower names InnoLight as a production partner (https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/tower-semiconductor-and-innolight-partner-to-develop-multi-generation-silicon). Q3 numbers also on AASTOCKS (https://www.aastocks.com/en/stocks/news/aafn-con/now.1552011/latest-news).

findings.finding: On 2026-10-13 Semtech expanded its multi-year SiGe agreement with Tower and is investing in dedicated SiGe capacity at Tower's fabs for AI data-center optical-interconnect parts. This is further prepaid or committed demand behind the SiGe ramp.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock closed +2.6% on 2026-10-13 (216.50 to 222.20) and fell the next day (209.16). Capacity deals have not held as catalysts in this tape.
findings.why_not_priced: The deal is public, but its dollar size and its effect on customer advances and the 2027 SiGe ramp will first appear in the Q3 balance sheet and on the call. If priced, the stock would not have fallen 27% since the announcement.
findings.independence: Separate from the InnoLight and 6-K findings. The GlobeNewswire original (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/10/13/3379474/0/en/tower-semiconductor-and-semtech-expand-sige-partnership-to-scale-power-efficient-analog-connectivity-for-data-centers.html) returned 403.

findings.finding: Q3 EPS: Q2 gross margin was about 29.9% (Q1 26.8%, Q2 2025 21.5%) and operating margin about 19.6% (Q1 15.6%), with the tax rate already at about 14.7%. Adding $60M of revenue at roughly 50% incremental operating margin gives about $1.08-1.12 adjusted EPS against the $1.05-1.07 consensus. That is a small beat, extending a five-quarter beat streak.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: EPS $0.88 versus $0.76 consensus and revenue $460.1M versus $454.7M. The stock closed +2.2% on 2026-08-04 after trading as low as $206.40 intraday, then fell 11.9% on 08-05. This name has sold its last beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS has already risen from $0.892 to $1.066 over 90 days (24/7), so most of the leverage is in the bar. What remains is a few cents, on a line this stock has not paid for.
findings.independence: Same 6-K as the guidance finding, but a different line (reported-quarter margin versus the Q4 guide). The estimate revision trend is from 24/7 (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/27/tower-semiconductors-1-2b-profit-roadmap-faces-its-biggest-test-yet-in-q3-earnings/).

findings.finding: A sector shock hit the AI-optics names on 2026-10-29/30. Alphabet reported Q3 free cash flow of -$9.1B against -$3.5B expected, though 2026 capex was unchanged at $195-205B. Intel guided Q4 to $15-16B against $17B expected and fell about 30%. COHR -13%, LITE -10%, AAOI -15%, and TSEM -14.1% to 161.36 with no company news. The print opens on Monday into this momentum.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In the 2026-05-13 print the stock went from a sector-driven dip into +22.6%. On 2026-08-04/05 a broader tech pullback swamped a beat (-11.9% the next day).
findings.why_not_priced: The Friday close already holds the shock (spot 161.36). What is left is whether de-risking continues into Monday's open, which the +20.7 put skew says the market expects. This is macro-to-company transmission; no Tower customer has cut. Alphabet kept 2026 capex unchanged and expects 2027 capex to rise significantly, so the demand line itself was not cut.
findings.independence: Alphabet capex unchanged and 2027 to rise significantly (https://fourweekmba.com/ai-google-cloud-revenue-doubles-to-30-7b-as-capex-hits-51-4b/), which cuts against reading this as a demand cut. Intel guide: https://qz.com/intel-stock-falls-revenue-forecast-pc-demand-102926.

findings.finding: CEO Russell Ellwanger sold 104,226 shares at $248.34 (about $25.9M, 16.5% of his holding) on 2026-08-11. Insiders sold about $45.6M over the quarter with no purchases.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measurable. The sale came a week after the Q2 print, at a price 54% above today's.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since August and widely republished, so largely priced. It matters only as context for how the CEO frames the Q4 guide.

findings.finding: Capex is running ahead of operating cash: Q2 net capex was $187M against $177M operating cash flow, with the $920M SiPho/SiGe program about 50% paid. The balance sheet funds it: about $1.48B of cash and deposits against $142M of debt, plus $321M of customer advances. Answer to the financing question: the money buys customer-prepaid capacity, so this is close to zero.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history of this line moving the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Q3 cash flow is unseen. If free cash flow turned clearly negative, it would echo the Alphabet free-cash-flow fear in a nervous tape, but net cash of $1.34B and prepayments make that a minor line.
findings.independence: Same 6-K as the guidance and EPS findings; a different line (cash flow).

findings.finding: The Intel New Mexico capacity agreement is in dispute resolution. Intel stated in February 2026 that it does not intend to perform, and the Q2 6-K still lists the dispute as a risk without quantifying it. Tower invested up to $300M in equipment at that site under the 2023 deal. A settlement or impairment could be disclosed with Q3, now that Intel is under fresh pressure (Q4 guide miss, Fab 28 outage).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-02-11, when the Intel non-performance was disclosed with Q4 2025 results: -1.6% close-to-close.
findings.why_not_priced: The outcome is unknown and either sign is possible: cash compensation, or a write-down of the New Mexico equipment. It is below operating income, and the volumes were rerouted to Fab 7 Japan, so there is no path to the guide. Sized at zero with a band.
findings.independence: TrendForce on the rerouting to Japan (https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/02/13/news-intel-reportedly-backs-out-of-300mm-wafer-deal-with-tower-production-could-move-to-japan/).

findings.finding: Bloomberg (via secondary reports, 2026-10-28) reports Marvell is in advanced all-stock talks to acquire Lumentum. Marvell is a named Tower SiPho partner; Lumentum is a laser/optics peer with its own photonics. Effect on Tower's customer mix is ambiguous.
findings.why_not_priced: Unconfirmed and could be announced the same week. Nothing ties it to Tower's Q4 volumes. Filed for completeness at zero.

findings.finding: STMicroelectronics, a specialty-analog peer and SiPho competitor, guided Q4 2026 revenue to $4.15B (+10.5% QoQ) with gross margin of 39.0%, versus Q3's 37.3%, on 2026-10-29. That points to recovery in the industrial/auto/power lines that make up most of Tower's non-SiPho revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history of Tower reacting to ST guides.
findings.why_not_priced: It was swamped by the 10-30 sector selloff. It is a proxy for the roughly 60% of Tower revenue outside SiPho (the net-of-rest check for the SiPho findings). ST also competes in SiPho with PIC100, which is a mild offset.
findings.independence: Separate document from all Tower and InnoLight sources.

outside_window.finding: Lumentum (reported 2026-11-05) and Coherent report after the window; their SiPho/transceiver commentary will reprice the optics group, Tower included.

baseline_tension: The company-level evidence (own Q4 targets, customer InnoLight's +24.6% QoQ with binding 2027 orders, Semtech capacity deal) leans mildly positive. That cuts against the +20.7 put skew and the -32% 20-day run-up, which are explained by a sector-wide AI-optics de-rating rather than any Tower-specific cut. Hence only a small lean (p_up 53), not a large one.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6/core table (inside what the company already guided): the Q4 guide finding was cut from +0.5 to +0.3, because Tower's own SiPho $1B Q4 target is what consensus is built from.
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; the Q2 beat was sold -11.9% the next day): the reported-quarter EPS finding was cut from +0.5 to +0.3.
Lesson 5 (proxy sized small): the InnoLight customer read-through was cut from +0.8 to +0.6, and the capacity constraint is stated in the finding.
Lesson 7 (sign against a strong skew): p_up moved from 55 to 53. Expected move fell from +1.3 to +0.78; the stated reason the skew may be wrong is that it prices sector momentum, not a company cut.
Lesson 8/core (understatement): abs_move_pct left at 13, above the 11.67% implied.
Last section (wrong-event history): reaction history rebuilt from confirmed print dates. This was already done in the draft; nothing changed.
